title: Podcast enclosure downloads bypass outbound URL safety checks

evidence.quote: url_value = item.get("url") or item.get("href") ... return url_value
async with httpx.AsyncClient(follow_redirects=True, timeout=120) as client: ... client.stream("GET", audio_url) ... f.write(chunk)

reasoning: Feed URLs and normal article URLs go through validate_public_url, but media enclosure URLs are accepted directly from untrusted RSS entries and downloaded with redirect following. A feed can point content_url at loopback/private metadata services or a huge file; the code neither validates the initial or redirected URL nor enforces a maximum download size before writing it to disk and invoking ffmpeg.
recommendation: Validate audio_url with the same public URL policy before download, use an httpx transport or redirect hook that re-validates each redirect target, restrict schemes to http/https, enforce a Content-Length and streamed byte limit, and fail closed before ffmpeg/transcription.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: tests/test_media_processor.py only verifies extension-based routing and stubs _process_audio for enclosures; tests/test_content_processor.py asserts public enclosure extraction but does not cover private-host, redirect, or oversized enclosure URLs.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an async MediaProcessor test with Settings(allow_private_hosts=False) and content_url='http://127.0.0.1/audio.mp3' asserting no httpx stream is opened and a safe error is returned; add a streaming fake that exceeds the byte cap and assert the download aborts.
minimumFixScope: app/services/media_processor.py plus a small helper or reuse of app.core.net validation; optionally validate content_url when extracted in app/services/content_processor.py.

history.reasoning: The original content_processor evidence still exists at app/services/content_processor.py:128-161 and still extracts enclosure/content URLs without validating them there, but the sink has changed. app/services/media_processor.py now imports validate_public_url, disables automatic redirects, validates the initial audio_url before opening a stream, validates each current_url and redirect target, limits redirects, checks Content-Length, and aborts streamed downloads over MAX_AUDIO_DOWNLOAD_BYTES before ffmpeg. Regression tests now exist in tests/test_media_processor.py for blocking private enclosure URLs before HTTP, blocking private redirect targets, and aborting oversized streams. The normal pytest command could not run in this read-only sandbox because Python/pytest had no usable temporary directory, so I ran no-write regression snippets that confirmed a 127.0.0.1 enclosure returns Audio download blocked without opening httpx, a redirect to 127.0.0.1 is blocked after only the public first request, and an oversized stream returns file too large before ffmpeg.
commands: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -c '<no-write regression snippet for private enclosure and private redirect target>'
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -c '<no-write regression snippet for oversized stream cap>'
